annotation.title_clean: Autonomous and Intelligent Robots: Social, Legal and Ethical Issues
annotation.title_en: Autonomous and Intelligent Robots: Social, Legal and Ethical Issues
annotation.venue: Multidisciplinary Perspectives on Artificial Intelligence and the Law (Springer, Law, Governance and Technology Series 58)
annotation.summary_en: Book chapter surveying industrial and service robots, defining robot autonomy and intelligence, and outlining social, ethical and legal concerns such as job displacement, privacy, human safety and trust. It notes robotics remains largely unregulated and calls for an ecosystem of researchers, companies and lawmakers to make robots trusted and secure.
key_provisions_or_claims: Distinguishes autonomous embodied robots from disembodied AI software, which raises distinct ethical and legal concerns.
Industrial robots mainly raised job-loss issues; service robots add safety, privacy and decision-making dilemmas.
Autonomous trucks and taxis may cause significant workforce displacement.
Robot markets remain largely unregulated; emerging AI legislation may serve as a safeguard.
Calls for multi-stakeholder ecosystem to build trusted, secure robots.
